n0001.title: On GPT-3: Scaling And Meta-Learning
n0001.gist: GPT-3 shows that simply scaling up neural networks yields meta-learning and validates the scaling hypothesis as a path to AGI.

n0002.title: On GPT-3: Meta-Learning And Scaling
n0002.gist: GPT-3’s massive scale enables few-shot meta-learning, proving that bigger models absorb data and compute to become more Bayesian.

n0003.title: Introduction And Summary
n0003.gist: The scaling hypothesis holds that neural nets generalize and become more Bayesian as they are scaled up on more data and compute.

n0006.title: Meta-Learning
n0006.gist: GPT-3 learns to follow directions and pick up new tasks from examples purely through next-word prediction at scale.

n0007.title: Meta-Learning
n0007.gist: GPT-3’s attention mechanisms act as fast weights, letting it solve diverse problems from prompts without finetuning.

n0010.title: Flexing GPT
n0010.gist: GPT-3 flexibly generates creative output like jokes and code, revealing meta-learning that standard NLP benchmarks fail to capture.

n0011.title: Flexing GPT
n0011.gist: GPT-3 is a small, shallow, dumbly-trained model that nevertheless manifests runtime meta-learning and generates surprisingly good samples.

n0016.title: Baking The Cake
n0016.gist: Unsupervised learning is finally rising as the foundation for AI, and scaling curves suggest heading to trillions of parameters remains useful.

n0017.title: Baking The Cake
n0017.gist: GPT-3 is just a text prediction model, but unsupervised learning is the cake that will support future systems like RL and robotics.

n0025.title: Scaling
n0025.gist: Scaling laws for loss remain predictable and continue past GPT-3, leaving plenty of room for further gains in capability.

n0026.title: Scaling
n0026.gist: The scaling curves have not bent; losses keep dropping logarithmically, so trillion-parameter models are feasible and benchmark gains will follow.

n0035.title: Blessings Of Scale
n0035.gist: Simply making models bigger induces stability, generalization, and meta-learning, as sub-models average out to prefer simple solutions.

n0036.title: Blessings Of Scale
n0036.gist: Bigger models and harder problems produce better learning, generalization, and meta-learning across many domains like images and robots.

n0043.title: Why Blessings Of Scale Exist
n0043.gist: Large models work by ensembling countless sub-models in a high-dimensional space, where Occam’s razor and enough data force genuine abstract solutions.

n0050.title: Scaling Hypothesis
n0050.gist: The scaling hypothesis claims that scaling up simple uniform architectures will naturally produce ever more sophisticated intelligence.

n0051.title: Scaling Hypothesis
n0051.gist: The author was wrong to doubt that scalable architectures would emerge; we built the compute and the algorithms did come.

n0055.title: Why Does Pretraining Work?
n0055.gist: Pretraining works because predicting human data exhaust forces models to learn causality and reasoning, and the last bits of loss are the deepest.

n0056.title: Pretraining Thesis And Early Learning
n0056.gist: Humans emit structured data, so a model predicting it must learn logic and causality, starting from letter frequencies to vocabulary.

n0062.title: Associations And Hard Training
n0062.gist: As training continues, models pick up word associations and subtle long-range dependencies, with errors becoming vanishingly rare.

n0070.title: The Last Bits Are Deepest
n0070.gist: The final drop to human-level loss requires true understanding, because rare and deeply consequential decisions depend on those last bits.

n0079.title: Doubts And Rebuttals
n0079.gist: Skeptics argued pretraining was a magic trick requiring impossible data, but Transformers and RNNs would have worked given enough compute.

n0084.title: Future Scaling Questions
n0084.gist: No one quantitatively predicted GPT-3’s loss drops, and no one knows what capabilities another 30% loss improvement would bring.

n0091.title: Prospects
n0091.gist: Future progress depends on conviction to scale, but labs like Google and DeepMind lack vision while OpenAI bets on the scaling hypothesis.

n0092.title: Prospects
n0092.gist: Wiener and Sutskever note that knowing a problem has an answer, plus conviction, is what's needed to pursue massive scale.

n0097.title: Hardware Overhang And Lab Visions
n0097.gist: The hardware overhang means only human conviction limits scaling, yet Google Brain is too practical and DeepMind pursues weak scaling.

n0103.title: OpenAI's Bet On Scaling
n0103.gist: OpenAI restructured to bet everything on scaling, but competitors lack the courage of their convictions and no model has yet matched GPT-3.

n0107.title: Critiquing The Critics
n0107.gist: Critics who dismissed deep learning were wrong, and their authority consists of phatic reassurance rather than predictive models.

n0108.title: Critiquing The Critics
n0108.gist: Only a few connectionists predicted deep learning’s success, and Moravec’s hardware-overhang forecasts have been vindicated.

n0114.title: Reductionism And Alchemy
n0114.gist: Dismissing AI as ‘just’ mechanisms misses that reductionism is how success must look, and researchers describe scaling as alchemy.

n0120.title: Authority Without Accountability
n0120.gist: Experts who endlessly predicted failure issue no mea culpas and speak in a bureaucratic tone that avoids falsifiable predictions.

n0126.title: Appendix
n0126.gist: The appendix marks the start of supplementary essays on GPT-3 and agency.

n0127.title: Appendix
n0127.gist: The appendix introduces further speculation on agency in language models.

n0129.title: It From Byte
n0129.gist: Generative models like GPT-3 inevitably become agents because agency is a useful continuum that emerges even from non-agentic data.

n0130.title: It From Byte
n0130.gist: GPT-3 does offline imitation learning from human data, so it learns to roleplay agents and can act in the real world via effectors.

n0138.title: All Is Atoms & Void
n0138.gist: Agency is constructed from non-agentic atoms, so simulating physics from the ground up could eventually reproduce agents.

n0142.title: Intentional Interpretive Stance
n0142.gist: Humans use the intentional stance to model natural systems as agents because it is predictively useful.

n0145.title: Variational Interpretations
n0145.gist: Variational principles let models treat systems as minimizing a reward, a shortcut that neural nets love and find universally useful.

n0152.title: Inducing Emergence Is Expensive
n0152.gist: Variational approaches are powerful but costly, so capabilities like agency only emerge with enough model size, data, and training.

n0155.title: What Can Induce Agency Emergence?
n0155.gist: Whether a dataset induces agency is an empirical question that we cannot currently answer a priori.

n0158.title: Cellular Automatons
n0158.gist: Even Conway’s Game of Life might induce an intentional stance, because chunking patterns into gliders is simpler than tracking cells.

n0164.title: Turing Machine
n0164.gist: Training on all Turing machines provides the most general computable setting for testing whether agency emerges.

n0167.title: Single TM
n0167.gist: A single random Turing machine seems harmless because it has nothing to optimize, so it probably induces no agency.

n0171.title: TM Meta-Learning
n0171.gist: Training over many Turing machines introduces a homunculus following instructions, which is a rudimentary theory of mind.

n0176.title: Ambient Agency
n0176.gist: Agency is a convergent capability that will emerge in sufficiently broad systems, so we must abandon the idea of safe tool AIs.
